materialReview.scope: Runtime inventory and native combat camera review.
materialReview.result: The exact renderer reports ftkmf_sablevine-palette.png as its main texture with native emission disabled. The selected frames show distinct palette bands, but camera crop rejects the current asset as a usable combat presentation.

selectedPNGs.observation: The full authored serpent binds to the exact native renderer, but the upper silhouette is already clipped by the combat camera.
A later idle sample retains its connected colored body and leaf forms, while confirming that the camera cannot frame the full upright creature.
The exact native Attack trigger is recorded at this transition; the visible lower body remains connected but the head region is off-screen.
The native attack clip visibly moves the lower body without a renderer loss, yet the cropped upper body prevents a usable full-silhouette review.
Attack follow-through retains the palette and bound mesh, but does not resolve the camera-fit rejection.
The exact ordinary player Damaged trigger is recorded while the renderer remains visible through the hit effect.
The received nonlethal hit keeps the visible body connected and shows no lost custom renderer.
Later hit recovery remains technically coherent, but the upper framing problem remains.
The separate explicit fixture records the exact native Death trigger while the bound model is still visible.
The native death path folds the visible body into a connected defeated pose; this is not ordinary lethal-damage or ragdoll evidence.
A later death sample still shows a coherent body on the floor before the native victory UI.

limits: This review covers the exact enbaseysnake / snakeJungleA / enSnake_Basey source pair only; direct Jungle Snake rows and sibling resource-prefab routes require their own trials.
V1 is explicitly rejected for native combat-camera fit because the upper body and head are cropped in normal idle and attack framing.
The ordinary hit is nonlethal; the separate explicit KillSingle transition is not ordinary lethal-damage acceptance.
The native death clip remains animator-driven and no rigidbodies were recorded, so this is not a ragdoll or settled-corpse review.
Culling envelope, portraits, long-session resource lifetime, other native ability variants, and final art-direction approval remain separate work.
